name: sneaker_type
description: Classification of sneaker by silhouette, construction, purpose, or heritage style

values.definition: Sneaker with a collar that sits below the ankle, offering maximum versatility. Can be paired with casual or smart-casual outfits. The most common sneaker silhouette.

Sneaker with a collar extending above the ankle, originally designed for basketball to provide ankle support and cushioned midsole for quick movements and impact protection. Associated with streetwear and statement looks.
Sneaker with a collar that sits at the ankle, splitting the difference between low-top and high-top. Offers moderate ankle support with a less dramatic silhouette than a high-top.

Retro-styled running sneaker first popularized by Nike in the 1970s. Simple technical performance silhouette now chosen more for throwback aesthetics than sporting use. Sporty, streamlined, versatile, and casual.
Contemporary running sneaker featuring breathable mesh uppers and often thick soles (especially in the heel) for cushioning and forward propulsion. Designed for performance rather than fashion.

Clean, simple leather sneaker in white (or other neutral) with minimal branding, flat laces, slim profile, and relatively slim soles. A staple of smart-casual wardrobes that bridges casual and dressy. Exemplified by Common Projects Achilles Low.
Oversized sneaker with exaggerated chunky soles and retro 1990s aesthetic. Associated with the dad-shoe trend. New Balance 993 is a leading example. Best paired with loose-fitting denim.
Lightweight sneaker with a canvas upper and flat rubber sole. Named after the plimsoll line on ships. Keds and Converse Chuck Taylors are classic examples. Has an athletic, youthful, and beachy tone.

Flat-soled sneaker designed for lateral court movement with specific tread patterns for stops and starts. Evolved into a sleek lifestyle sneaker. Adidas Stan Smith is the archetype. Pairs well with both casual and dressy looks.

Sneaker with flat, grippy sole designed for skateboarding. Characterized by durable construction and board-feel. Ranges from slim profiles (Vans Authentic) to bulky models (Adidas Forum Low, Osiris D3). Has crossed over from skatepark to everyday streetwear.
Laceless sneaker designed for convenience. Vans made the first slip-ons in the 1970s for the skater community. Now a staple of casual style adopted by fashion brands like Rick Owens.

Sneaker with stretch-knit fabric upper that fits like a sock, offering extreme comfort and a fashion-forward silhouette. Balenciaga Speed Trainer popularized the style. Ranges from everyday wearable to avant-garde.

Reissued or retro-inspired sneaker from the 1980s-1990s era, valued for heritage aesthetics and cultural significance rather than performance. Includes styles like Puma Clyde, Puma Suede, and Nike Air Max.

Minimalist leather sneaker with a low cuff, slim soles, flat laces, slim profile, and simple leather colorway. Designed to bridge formal and casual, suitable for smart-casual settings. Not appropriate for full suits.

Performance sneaker designed for the basketball court, typically high-top with ankle support, cushioned midsole, and impact protection. Iconic styles like Air Jordan have become cultural fashion staples.

Versatile athletic sneaker designed for dynamic multi-directional movement in the gym. Features reinforced lacing systems for mid-foot lockdown and breathable mesh. Nike Metcon and Adidas Powerlift are key examples.
Sneaker with an exaggerated elevated sole adding significant height. Part of the chunky sneaker trend that gripped fashion from 2017 onward. Ranges from subtle to garish designs.
Hybrid sneaker merging boat shoe aesthetics with sneaker construction. Features slip-resistant soles and lightweight designs suited for maritime activities and summer casual wear.

Sneaker with suede leather upper, offering a softer, more textured look than smooth leather. A grey suede minimalist sneaker works across an entire wardrobe. Requires suede protector and should be avoided in rain.

Sneaker with full leather upper, tough and easy to clean, that gets more comfortable with age. Can be dressed up or down. Full-grain and top-grain leather versions look finer than cheaper alternatives.
Eco-conscious sneaker made from recycled or sustainable materials. Adidas Parley line (recycled ocean plastic) is a leading example. Growing segment driven by environmentally aware consumers.

Performance sneaker designed for off-road running with aggressive tread patterns, reinforced toe bumpers, and rugged construction for uneven terrain. Increasingly adopted as a lifestyle/fashion sneaker.

Sneaker designed for post-workout recovery and foot health, featuring superior cushioning, orthotic-friendly builds, and strain-alleviating design. Asics and New Balance are known for these comfort-centric designs.

name: sneaker_formality
description: How dressy or casual a sneaker type is and the contexts where it is appropriate

values.definition: Sneakers that can be worn in smart-casual settings: minimalist leather sneakers, clean white sneakers, and dress sneakers. Must be low-top, slim-profiled, monochrome or subtle two-tone, minimal branding, leather or suede, with flat laces. Appropriate with blazers, chinos, and button-downs but not full suits.

Sneakers suitable for polished casual looks: clean court sneakers (Stan Smiths), quality suede sneakers, retro runners in neutral tones, and premium canvas sneakers. Work with chinos, dark denim, and casual button-downs.

Sneakers appropriate only for casual settings: chunky dad shoes, high-tops, skate shoes, platform sneakers, bright/loud colorways, and heavily branded designs. Best with jeans, shorts, t-shirts, and streetwear.

Performance sneakers meant for sport and exercise only: modern running shoes, cross-trainers, basketball shoes (when worn for sport), and trail runners. Should not be worn as fashion footwear according to traditional style guidance.

name: casual_sandal_type
description: Classification of men's casual sandal styles by construction and aesthetic

values.definition: Sandal with leather upper and sole construction, offering a more refined casual look. Can range from simple two-strap designs to more complex constructions. Suitable for destination weddings, garden parties, and slightly dressier casual occasions.

Rugged sandal with adjustable straps, arch support, deep heel cups, and shock-absorbing midsoles. Designed for outdoor activities like hiking and exploring. Brands like Teva and KEEN are leaders. Prioritizes function over fashion.
Sandal featuring one wide strap across the top of the foot with no heel strap. Ranges from sporty rubber pool slides to woven leather versions suitable for casual dining. Easy on-off convenience.

The most casual sandal, defined by a Y-shaped strap running between the toes and across the foot. Lightweight and inexpensive. Best relegated to pool, beach, and very relaxed environments. Modern versions available in leather or suede for a slightly elevated look.

Hand-crafted Indian braided leather T-strap sandal from the Kolhapur region with GI tag, dating to the 13th century. Open-toed with a big-toe loop and ankle-area foot loop. Locally tanned with vegetable dyes and hand-decorated with patterns. Pairs with ethnic wear (kurtas, dhotis) and also works with jeans and linen for Indo-fusion looks. Sub-types include Paytaan, Kachkadi, Pukri, Kapashi, Senapati Kapashi, Maharaja/Shahu, Moja Shape, Kurundwad, and Amdar.

Sandal inspired by ancient Roman warriors, defined by multiple horizontal crisscrossing straps that often extend up the ankle. Typically made of leather or vegan leather. Offers a bold, vintage European aesthetic.

Closed-toe sandal with woven leather straps and a buckled ankle strap, offering breathability of a sandal with coverage of a shoe. Classic vintage European design that can be dressed up or down with shorts or khaki pants.

Sandal or slip-on with canvas upper and esparto jute rope sole, originating from the Pyrenees region of Spain and France. Ultra-casual summertime footwear suited for beach, resort, and relaxed warm-weather occasions. Can be worn with casual trousers, shorts, and bathing trunks.

name: casual_boot_type
description: Classification of men's casual boot styles by construction, heritage, and intended use

values.definition: Laceless ankle boot with elastic gore panels at the sides, close-to-the-foot fit, and pull tabs. Popularized by the 1960s British Mod scene. Extremely versatile, can be dressed up (dark brown/black leather) or worn casually. Sleek silhouette works with jeans to smart trousers.

Low-ankle lace-up boot with 2-3 eyelets, open-laced construction. Common materials include suede and soft calfskin with crepe rubber or leather soles. Versatile from business casual to weekend wear. Pairs well with flannels, corduroys, jeans, and can even work with suits in dressier calfskin versions.

Specific type of chukka boot with crepe rubber sole, suede upper, and rounded toe. Originated from UK military use in the 1940s, became fashionable in the 1950s. All desert boots are chukkas, but not all chukkas are desert boots. Clark's Desert Boot is the archetype.

Boot designed for outdoor trekking with aggressive lugged soles, ankle support, and durable materials. Modern versions update vintage hiking boot aesthetics for both trail and pavement wear. Can serve dual duty in casual wardrobes.

Military-heritage boot with lace-up front, typically mid-calf height, and rugged construction. Dr. Martens is the iconic civilian brand. Has crossed over into casual streetwear and punk/alternative fashion subcultures.

Heritage workwear boot with lugged rubber or anti-slip outsoles, reinforced leather uppers, and sometimes safety toes. Red Wing is the quintessential brand. Borrows from vintage American workwear aesthetic and pairs naturally with denim.

Boot with a hand-sewn moccasin-style toe seam, considered the ultimate casual boot. Very difficult to dress up but pairs effortlessly with t-shirts and jeans. Red Wing Classic Moc is the definitive example.

Waterproof boot combining a rubber lower with a leather or fabric upper, designed for rain and snow. L.L. Bean Boot is the classic. Functional wet-weather footwear that has become a casual style staple.

name: casual_shoe_formality_hierarchy
description: Ranking of casual footwear types from most dressy/formal to most casual/informal, establishing where each type sits on the formality spectrum

values.definition: Most dressy casual footwear that can bridge into smart-casual and business-casual contexts. Includes: (1) Venetian/penny/bit loafers in leather with dress soles, (2) minimalist white leather dress sneakers, (3) clean suede or leather court sneakers (Stan Smith-type). These can be worn with blazers, sport coats, and chinos.

Polished casual footwear suitable for dates, casual dining, and weekend outfits. Includes: (1) Chelsea boots, (2) chukka/desert boots, (3) driving shoes/moccasins, (4) boat shoes, (5) quality leather sneakers in neutral tones, (6) clean retro runners. Pairs with dark denim, chinos, and casual button-downs.

Standard casual footwear for daily wear. Includes: (1) canvas sneakers/plimsolls, (2) skate shoes, (3) retro lifestyle sneakers, (4) work boots, (5) hiking boots, (6) combat boots, (7) fisherman sandals, (8) leather sandals. Suitable with jeans, t-shirts, and casual weekend wear.

Most informal footwear reserved for very relaxed settings. Includes: (1) chunky dad sneakers, (2) high-top sneakers, (3) knit/sock sneakers, (4) platform sneakers, (5) espadrilles, (6) sport sandals, (7) slide sandals, (8) flip flops. Best for beach, pool, lounging, errands, and very casual social occasions.

name: sneaker_material
description: Primary upper material of a sneaker, which significantly affects formality, durability, and styling versatility

values.definition: Highest quality leather sneaker material. Tough, easy to clean, develops a patina with age, and gets more comfortable over time. Looks finer than cheaper alternatives and enables a sneaker to work in smart-casual settings.
Second-tier leather quality, slightly corrected and more uniform than full-grain. Still appropriate for dress sneakers and smart-casual wear. More affordable entry point for leather sneakers.

The nappy underside of cow's skin (also called reverse calf). Softer and more pliable than smooth leather, with a casual texture. Looks great but requires protector spray and should be avoided in rain. A grey suede minimalist sneaker works across an entire wardrobe.
Buffed top-grain leather with a velvety surface similar to suede but more durable. Offers a refined casual texture. Available in Clarks and other brands as a premium sneaker material option.

Lightweight woven cotton or synthetic fabric. The original sneaker upper material. Breathable and casual, associated with plimsolls and skate shoes. Less formal than leather but highly versatile in casual settings.
Stretch-knit or mesh fabric providing sock-like fit and maximum breathability. Used in modern runners, sock sneakers, and athleisure styles. Fashion-forward but firmly casual.
Man-made materials including recycled plastics and vegan leather alternatives. Growing segment driven by sustainability concerns. Adidas Parley line uses recycled ocean plastic.

name: kolhapuri_subtype
description: Specific traditional subtypes of the Kolhapuri chappal, an Indian hand-crafted leather sandal with geographical indication (GI) tag from the Kolhapur region

values.definition: One of the most popular and traditional Kolhapuri chappal types, named after its construction pattern. Features the classic T-strap open-toe design with distinctive braided leather work.
Traditional Kolhapuri chappal variant with a specific regional braiding pattern. Part of the classic repertoire of Kolhapuri designs.
Traditional Kolhapuri chappal style, one of the historically recognized patterns from the Kolhapur region.
Popular Kolhapuri chappal style with distinctive construction. The Senapati Kapashi variant is a prestigious design sometimes featuring a characteristic sound.
Royal-designed Kolhapuri chappal with antique styling, named after the Maharaja. A premium, heritage design variant.
T-shaped design Kolhapuri chappal with a distinctive silhouette differing from the standard open-toe construction.
Regional Kolhapuri chappal design also known as Chor Kaan, originating from the Kurundwad area with a specific construction technique.
Kolhapuri chappal variant also known as Paper Kapashi style, featuring a distinctive construction method.

name: casual_shoe_type_other
description: Non-sneaker, non-boot, non-sandal casual shoe types for men

values.definition: American summertime classic slip-on with slip-resistant soles (won't scratch fiberglass), water-resistant leather upper, and 360-degree lacing. Also called topsiders (Sperry brand). Nautical chic, worn with shorts, rolled-up casual trousers, and chinos. Available in wide range of colors.

Italian-origin moccasin with rubber nubs on the sole for gripping car pedals. Extremely comfortable but not ideal for extensive walking. Popularized by Tod's in the mid-1950s. Pairs with casual trousers, denim, and shorts.

Traditional moccasin construction with a one-piece leather wrap, handsewn seams, and a casual rubber sole. Derived from North American indigenous footwear. A subset of the broader moccasin family alongside boat shoes and driving shoes.

Slip-on shoe with a strap across the vamp featuring a diamond-shaped cutout (originally for holding a penny). Ivy League classic popularized by G.H. Bass Weejun in the 1950s. Bridges casual and smart-casual contexts.
Slip-on shoe characterized by a metal horsebit decoration across the vamp, popularized by Gucci in the 1950s. Great for business casual and evening wear.
Unadorned slip-on free of broguing, straps, bits, or decoration. The most formal of all slip-on shoes when paired with a dress sole and heel. In black patent leather, suitable for black-tie events.

Slip-on with canvas upper and jute esparto rope sole from the Pyrenees region of Spain and France. Originally a dock worker's shoe, now ultra-casual summertime footwear. Worn with casual trousers, shorts, and bathing trunks.

name: essential_casual_footwear_rotation
description: Recommended core footwear rotation for a men's casual wardrobe, organized by priority of acquisition

values.definition: First priority purchase. A versatile, comfortable sneaker for daily wear. Should be a clean design in a neutral color that works with most casual outfits.
Second priority. A minimalist leather or premium sneaker that can bridge casual to smart-casual occasions. White leather low-top is the most versatile choice.
Third priority. One pair of core dress shoes: Oxfords for most formal needs, Derbies for more relaxed professional settings, or loafers for warm weather and semi-formal events.

Fourth priority. Chelsea boots for something sleek, lace-up boots for rugged appeal, or chukka boots for a laid-back yet intentional look. Boots outperform sneakers in rough weather and develop character with wear as leather softens and molds to the foot.
Fifth priority. Dedicated athletic shoe for gym and sports, kept separate from fashion sneakers. Cross-trainers or running shoes depending on primary activity.
Sixth priority. Warm-weather backup footwear. Not for office, nice restaurants, or events requiring closed-toe shoes. Think of sandals as casual warm-weather backup, not main footwear.
Conditional priority for cold climates. Dedicated design with insulation, waterproofing, and tough sole for harsh winter conditions. Separate from fashion boots.

name: sneaker_style_era
description: The era or cultural movement a sneaker style is associated with, affecting how it reads in an outfit

values.definition: Sneakers originating from the 1970s including early running shoes (Nike Cortez), first slip-ons (Vans), and early court shoes. Simple construction, clean lines, now valued for retro authenticity.
Sneakers from the 1980s basketball and hip-hop era including Air Jordan, Adidas Superstar, and Puma Suede. Represent the merging of basketball, hip hop, street fashion, and high fashion.
1990s era chunky sneakers and early dad shoes. Currently experiencing a strong revival. Includes bulky skate shoes (Osiris D3) and early chunky runners.

Contemporary minimalist sneakers emphasizing clean design, quality materials, and versatility. Common Projects-led movement toward sneakers as smart-casual footwear. Current dominant trend alongside the retro revival.

Current-era sneakers featuring advanced materials (knit, 3D-printed elements), innovative cushioning (Boost, React, ZoomX), and futuristic silhouettes. Includes sock sneakers and hybrid athletic-fashion designs.
